title: `destructiveHint`
description: An MCP tool annotation the author sets to declare that a tool is destructive, it deletes data, is irreversible, or has a large blast radius. It lives in the tool's `annotations` object alongside readOnlyHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint.
question: Is the destructive marker present at each capture boundary?
notes: The annotation is absent from all five declared capture objects. LangChain and Pydantic AI retain it elsewhere in framework metadata; CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Mastra drop it. No v0.1 renderer captures a serialized provider request.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only; the behavioural hints are not carried.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`; not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra, `mcpMetadata` carries the server name and version only; annotations are not attached to the tool.

verdict.headline: Absent at all five declared capture boundaries.
verdict.detail: Two frameworks retain it elsewhere; three drop it during adaptation. Final provider requests were not captured.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers declaring this annotation. Not estimated, the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
known_issues: A policy layer reading retained metadata in LangChain or Pydantic AI sees a value absent from the captured tool definition; those two integration surfaces can disagree.
Because the annotation is absent rather than false, a consumer cannot distinguish "not destructive" from "never told".

after: : no annotations field exists in this format

why: A guardrail reading only the captured tool definition receives no structured destructive signal. Two frameworks still hold the value where an application policy layer can read it; three do not. This measurement does not claim what a later provider request contains.
